levels.technical:
At mean-field level. The two-mode block $H = K(n_a + n_c) + \mu w_aw_c + \mu^*v_cv_a$ with $\mu \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ is self-adjoint, with $\operatorname{ad}_H^2 = K^2 + |\mu|^2$ on all four mode operators and block spectrum $\{K - E, K, K, K + E\}$, $E = \sqrt{K^2 + |\mu|^2}$; with $\mu = mB$, $B = B_N(f(k), f(-k))$ the mass pairing of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.mass} on unit-normalised plane-wave modes ($|B| = 1$), the dispersion is $E^2 = K^2 + m^2$. The tower element $H_4 = \sum_b K(n_a + n_c) - GP^*P$, $P = \sum_b w_aw_c$, is self-adjoint, conserves the axial number and has exact pair states of energy $2Kn - Gn(n_b - n + 1)$; pairs enter the ground state exactly when $G > 2K/n_b$, the threshold of the mean-field energy.

In the block ground state $\langle w_aw_c\rangle = -\mu^*/(2E)$, so the gap equation holds: the fermion mass is $G$ times the pair condensate. The axial phase is an inner unitary of the tower, $UH(\mu)U^* = H(\mu e^{-2\theta I_4})$, so the mean-field energy has an exactly flat phase direction.
levels.lay: A pair of fermion modes in the tower can bind into a scalar condensate that gives the fermions mass, the mechanism of Nambu and Jona-Lasinio. At mean-field level these exact computations reproduce its ingredients: the massive energy relation, the coupling above which pairs condense, the gap equation, and a direction in which the condensate's phase can turn at no cost.
levels.one-liner: At mean-field level the tower reproduces the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio mechanism: a self-adjoint mass block with $E^2 = K^2 + m^2$, pairing above $G = 2K/n_b$, the gap equation and a flat axial phase.

proofs.main: Proof by exact computation: \texttt{ga\_bosons\_2026-10-16}, S1.1 to S3 and S2.5. Mean field only; the massless pole is the imported random-phase result; at finite size the exact ground state has $\langle P\rangle = 0$; the order parameter is a Lorentz scalar but a single shell is frame-dependent; the axial $U(1)$ is anomalous, so with colour the scalar is massive.
